source_text: Deus autem spei repleat vos omni gaudio et pace in credendo, ut abundetis in spe in virtute Spiritus sancti. Gloria Christo Iesu in saecula. Amen.
thought_title: A prayer for hope, joy, and peace
orientation: Origen has just quoted Paul's words about the word of faith and confession, and now he closes this opening section with a prayer drawn from Romans 15:13.
pass_a_gloss: God however of hope may fill you [with] all joy and peace in believing, so that you may abound in hope in [the] power of [the] Spirit holy. Glory [to] Christ Jesus into [the] ages. Amen.

choices.english: But may the God of hope
choices.why: The genitive 'spei' modifies 'Deus' as a characteristic quality; 'autem' marks a transition and is rendered as 'But' to preserve the connective force.
The gerund in the ablative with 'in' expresses the sphere or activity in which joy and peace are experienced; 'believing' keeps the verbal force rather than substituting the noun 'faith'.

choices.english: in the power of the Holy Spirit
choices.why: The phrase names the source of power for abounding in hope; 'Holy Spirit' is the natural English rendering of 'Spiritus sancti' in a doxological context.
rejected: in the power of the holy Spirit
by the power of the Holy Spirit

choices.why: The plural 'saecula' with 'in' is a standard doxological formula meaning endless ages; 'forever' conveys the sense naturally in English.

bible_refs.note: Deus autem spei repleat vos omni gaudio et pace in credendo, ut abundetis in spe in virtute Spiritus sancti

pass_b_english: But may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that you may abound in hope in the power of the Holy Spirit (Romans 15:13). Glory to Christ Jesus forever. Amen.

last_rejected.why: Glossary bans 'the Holy Spirit' for Spiritus; must be 'the Spirit'.
last_rejected.fix: in the power of the Spirit
last_rejected.ruling: 'Spiritus sancti' naturally renders as 'the Holy Spirit'; no meaning is changed or lost.
